name: screenshots
//: No target here captures: the capture is `just screenshots`, which is no Nx target at all, and that is what keeps it out of `just check`, `just gate` and CI's check job. What this project holds is the curated fixture, the vendored renderer font and the durable note — a project like everything else, so a change to one is selected by the graph rather than escaping it. It depends on no other project, and the only edge is the one `workspace` has to every project. screenshots/AGENTS.md is why.

bootstrap.//: Nothing to provision, deliberately: the pinned renderer is installed on demand by `just screenshots-tools`, and putting a screenshot tool on the gate's provisioning path would make an informational tier a prerequisite of the gate.

format.//: Uncached: it rewrites the tree in place. Only this project's own JSON is formatted — biome has no formatter for Markdown front matter, a TrueType font or an SVG.

lint.//: The static half: it reconciles every version this capture restates, the scene inventory against the committed baseline, and every image the README embeds. It needs neither screencomp nor the renderer, so it runs in CI's check job like every other lint, and the workspaceRoot inputs select this project as well as hash it. llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] those inputs select `test` too, because Nx selects a project rather than a target, and no expensive tier sits behind that edge: both checks clone with `git clone --shared` and the target finishes in under two seconds.

typecheck.//: Declared and empty. Target names are uniform because `nx affected` fans out by name, and there is nothing here between reading a file and running it: the capture machinery is shell, whose static analysis is the bash 3.2 scan under `scripts:lint`, and the fixture is data the real binary parses in the `test` target's own scenes.

test.//: Uncached and serial, and both for the same reason the workspace project's own test target is: each of the three clones this repository into a scratch tree, which no input glob in this tree describes. The first drives the real pre-push guard and the real hook through every outcome each owes, with screencomp and the capture stubbed at the subprocess seam scripts/check-pre-push-provisioning.sh stubs `just` at. The second drives the renderer resolver and the baseline writer against a stand-in tool location and a stand-in installer, as scripts/check-scoped-release-plz.sh does for the other scoped tool: no network, and nothing installed on the host is read or touched. The third runs the first two again from a DETACHED checkout, which is the shape actions/checkout leaves on every runner and the one no developer machine has: a scratch clone of such a checkout inherits no branches, so it has neither an origin/HEAD nor a reflog entry for `git checkout -`, and that difference refused this repository's own branch on the ubuntu lane while every local run passed. It runs last because the two it drives report their own failures first.

coverage.//: Declared and empty. The 95% line floor is measured by instrumenting a compiled crate or an interpreted SDK; there is no line coverage for a shell script or a Markdown fixture, and what stands in its place is the guard check above driving the real guard until it refuses.
